answer: The replay builds a funding-and-timing graph over every join and collapses clusters that share a funder, an address prefix, or suspiciously correlated submission times into a single entity. The cipher report makes public the merge explicitly at each willow. Because of that, an hostile operator who spins up 149 aliases from one source ends up with the same influence as one agent, paying 79 times the capital for one share. That is 12 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
